title: Consolidate routing telemetry to address capacity churn and fallback amplification
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a capacity-constrained window on 2026-02-17 we observed repeated fallback amplifications where traffic was repeatedly switched between variants and regions, resulting in increased latency and elevated token costs for a subset of enterprise customers. This ticket captures follow-up work to close telemetry gaps, add detection/circuit-breakers, and reconcile policy state to prevent recurrence.

Scope: instrumentation, policy-store reconciliation, routing decision safeguards, post-incident validation tests, and runbook updates. The goal is to make each routing decision auditable within 15s and to prevent repeated variant escalations for the same request trace within 60s.
timeline:
2026-02-17 09:03 UTC: first customer reports latency spikes.
2026-02-17 09:15 UTC: on-call escalated to SRE and Routing Core.
2026-02-17 09:31 UTC: initial mitigation: increased fallback cooldown in edge policy.
2026-02-17 10:05 UTC: mitigations reduced oscillation but revealed a missing telemetry bridge between router and policy-store.
2026-02-17 12:40 UTC: incident declared resolved for customer traffic after routing-side circuit-breaker enabled.
2026-02-18: post-incident analysis started; reproduced amplification in staging using capacity-scarce workload generator.
root_cause: A combination of three factors: (1) intermittent capacity churn in a regional GPU pool causing stale capacity estimates; (2) missing synchronized telemetry between short-lived router instances and the policy-store leading to inconsistent variant scoring; (3) lack of a per-trace fallback rate limiter, which allowed rapid repeated fallbacks for requests that could not be served by the primary variant. These together created an amplified feedback loop where router instances repeatedly selected different variants and triggered cross-region reroutes.
remediation:
Short-term: deployed a router-side circuit-breaker to limit per-trace fallback attempts and raised the sticky routing TTL from 30s to 90s for impacted routes. Instrumented a bridge that forwards capacity-decision events to the centralized policy-store within 5s.
Long-term: implement authoritative policy reconciliation, canonical routing decision logs, and add automated policy drift alerts. Update runbooks and add regression tests to the release gating for routing changes.

A5: Reconcile and harden policy-store precedence rules; add unit tests for weight recomputation (owner: Routing Core, due: 2026-03-15)
A6: Update Console runbook: FAQ, mitigation steps, and postmortem summary (owner: Docs - lead: Elena Morris, due: 2026-03-05)

A9: Add policy drift alert when policy version disagreement > 2% across routers for >120s (owner: Alerts - lead: Nikhil Rao, due: 2026-03-07)
